**The Weight of a Single Leaf**

I remember the first time I noticed how much a single leaf could weigh. It wasn’t until I held one in my palm, the way the sunlight caught its edges, that I realized how fragile yet heavy it was. The weight of a leaf isn’t just in its substance—it’s in the way it bends under the wind, the way it clings to the branch like a secret.

I thought about how leaves carry the weight of the sky. They don’t complain, but they don’t ignore it either. They just *are*, suspended between the earth and the clouds, waiting for the right moment to fall. Some leaves last a season, others a day. But even the shortest-lived carry the memory of their time here.

I wonder if leaves ever think about the trees they once were. Or if they just let the wind do the work.

And then I thought about how we are like leaves—carrying the weight of our pasts, the weight of our futures, and sometimes, just the weight of the moment. We don’t always know why we’re here, but we keep going anyway.

Maybe that’s the secret of a leaf. It doesn’t ask questions. It just falls when it’s time.

And so do we.
